A kinetic group says "these steps share their rate constants", which requires lining up forward with forward. The edge case is a group of steps that do chemistry and change conformation, for example E(S) <--> F(P) and F(S) <--> E(P).

Aligned by chemistry (S → P forward in both, today's rule), the conformation runs E→F in one member and F→E in the other. Aligned by conformation (E→F in both), one member's S → P constant is tied to the other's P → S constant. The two give different models; in the probe v differed by up to 101%.

I recommend chemistry: a kinetic group means the same chemical step in two contexts, and the conformation label is secondary. Only hand-written mechanisms can reach this, because the enumerator builds conformation E only.
